sources.note: Manual counsellor review required; verify the correct F-1 (academic/language) or M-1 (vocational) category, exact SEVP-certified school and programme, admission and SEVIS registration, Form I-20 details/signatures, SEVIS I-901 fee receipt, DS-160 confirmation, current visa application fee and Colombo post instructions. Interview evidence may include academic preparation, intent to depart after the authorised study, and credible funds for tuition, living and travel costs. There is no single universal government bank-balance figure: reconcile evidence with the school's I-20 cost estimate and the student's funding plan. New F/M visas may be issued up to 365 days before course start, but entry is not permitted more than 30 days before the start date. A visa does not guarantee admission at the border. Check current State Department and school/DSO instructions; detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.note: Official UAE Government overview of student residence sponsorship routes. Automated check is availability-only (no page text comparison) because the portal timed out during content retrieval. Manually verify current wording and applicant-specific sponsorship with the accredited institution and relevant authority; for Dubai student residence permit requirements, use the GDRFA Dubai student service as the primary operational source.

German Embassy Colombo — Students (national visa)
German Embassy Colombo — Long-stay national visa requirements
Department of Home Affairs — Student visa condition 8105 (work limitation)
sources.note: Primary official condition page. Verify the visa grant notice and VEVO for the individual applicant; current published guidance describes the 48-hours-per-fortnight limit, exceptions and course-session rules. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: IRCC — Work off campus as an international student (24-hour weekly limit)
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual review required. Confirm the 24-hour weekly limit during regular academic sessions, eligibility (DLI, full-time status, programme at least 6 months leading to degree/diploma/certificate, studies started, permit conditions and SIN), and exclusions for ESL/FSL, general-interest and prerequisite-only courses. Scheduled breaks must be school-scheduled and at least 7 consecutive days; unlimited off-campus work is limited to 180 days per calendar year and no more than 150 consecutive days in back-to-back breaks. Check the official DLI calendar and permit conditions. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: IRCC — Proof of financial support (living-cost table)
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manually verify the current application-date threshold, family size, Quebec rules, tuition/travel exclusion and source-of-funds evidence.

sources.name: Make it in Germany — Visa for studying (2026 funds and student work)
sources.note: Federal Government guidance: check current blocked-account amount and student work limits; distinguish study visa from visa to seek a place and verify individual residence conditions.

sources.name: Immigration New Zealand — Working on a student visa
sources.note: Official student work eligibility and conditions; 25-hour limit applies only where the student's visa and course conditions permit it. Verify eVisa/visa letter.

sources.name: Immigration New Zealand — Changes to student visas (27 October 2026)
sources.note: Official INZ announcement of changes effective 27 October 2026: master's-by-research work-rights change for new applications, English-language ability as a key factor, broader processing suspension grounds, and extension of relevant post-course expiry period from 1 month to 2 months. Check application-date scope and current visa conditions; detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: IRCC — PAL/TAL requirements, exemptions and validity (2026)
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual review required for 2026 PAL/TAL cap-year validity, public DLI degree-granting master's/doctoral exemption from 1 January 2026, Quebec CAQ, school/level changes and other exceptions. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: IRCC — Post-graduation work permit eligibility
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual case review required. General tests: eligible DLI and exact PGWP-eligible programme; programme at least 8 months (900 hours for Quebec); full-time status each semester except possible part-time final semester; apply within 180 days of completion confirmation; verify study permit/status, authorised leave, transfers, distance learning, prior PGWP and exclusions including ESL/FSL, general-interest/non-credit and public-private curriculum-licensing partnership programmes. Language: bachelor's/master's/doctoral and other university graduates CLB/NCLC 7 in all 4 skills; college/polytechnic and other non-university graduates CLB/NCLC 5 in all 4 skills. For study permit applications on/after 1 Nov 2024, non-degree university and college/non-university programmes generally also need eligible field of study; bachelor's/master's/doctoral degrees have no field restriction. Check exact 6-digit CIP 2021 code and current 2026 frozen eligible list where applicable. Duration is not automatic: usually programme length for eligible programmes under 2 years, up to 3 years for eligible programmes 2 years or longer; eligible master's of at least 8 months may qualify for up to 3 years. Passport expiry can shorten validity. Detection is not legal interpretation; never promise PGWP or a fixed duration from a course title.

sources.name: IRCC — PGWP field of study and eligible CIP codes
sources.note: Availability-only automated check. IRCC states the eligible-field list is frozen for 2026; manually verify exact 6-digit CIP 2021 code, applicant's study permit/PGWP application dates and any grandfathering against the live official list. Do not infer eligibility from a programme title.

sources.name: IRCC — Designated learning institutions list and PGWP-eligible programme details
sources.note: Availability-only automated check. Manually verify exact institution, DLI number, province/campus, PGWP-eligible DLI list and exact programme details. IRCC explicitly states not all programmes at a listed DLI qualify. Cross-check all general PGWP, language and field-of-study requirements. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: UK Home Office — Register of licensed sponsors: Students
sources.note: Availability-only automated check. Manually verify legal sponsor name, Student sponsor category, rating and current licence status close to application; confirm exact course/CAS and sponsor remains licensed. The register was updated 11 November 2026 when checked.

sources.name: GOV.UK — Student visa: course requirements and CAS
sources.note: Availability-only automated check. Verify exact course level, mode, study location, approved qualification, ATAS if applicable, CAS details and 6-month application window. Do not treat an offer as a CAS.

sources.name: Australian Government — CRICOS registration
sources.note: Availability-only automated check. Verify provider and exact course CRICOS registration, campus/location, course code and registration dates; provider registration alone does not establish every course/campus is registered.

sources.name: Immigration New Zealand — Rules for approved education providers and Code signatories
sources.note: Availability-only automated check. Verify provider's current Code of Practice signatory status through NZQA and exact programme/campus; international students cannot study at a non-signatory institution. Provider status is not visa approval.

sources.name: Dubai Government — Student Residence Visa
sources.note: Official Dubai Government overview. Manually verify the exact institution, host/guarantor, campus, study programme and current GDRFA route. Institution host/guarantor status is not automatic for every course or provider.

sources.name: Visit Dubai — Apply for a student visa
sources.note: Dubai's official destination portal explains the institution-managed GDRFA process and typical applicant documents. Treat as guidance; confirm exact requirements and fees through the institution and GDRFA for the applicant's case.

sources.name: Federal ICP — Issuing residency permit (student conditions and documents)
sources.note: Official ICP service page. It lists student-specific documents, programme-based residence duration and a 180-day stay after completion of the study period. Do not conflate with GDRFA Dubai's 60-day statement after expiry/cancellation; confirm emirate, permit category and circumstances.

sources.name: MoHRE — Cabinet Resolution / Executive Regulations (student training and employment permit category)
sources.note: Official MoHRE-hosted executive regulations identify a student training and employment permit category for students already in the UAE, subject to conditions and employer approval. Verify current permit process, employer jurisdiction and eligibility before any work begins.

sources.name: GDRFA Dubai — Issuing a visit visa for study, training or rehabilitation
sources.note: Separate single-entry 30/60/180-day study or training visit-visa route. Verify host letter, passport validity, purpose, duration, extension and live fees. Do not confuse with student residence permit.

sources.name: GDRFA Dubai — Golden Residence for top students and graduates
sources.note: Exceptional 10-year merit-based residence category. Manually verify grade/GPA, graduation date, university ranking, certificate authentication and ICP/local nomination approval; not a standard student visa benefit.

sources.name: German Embassy Colombo — Opening / unblocking a blocked account
sources.note: Official Colombo mission guidance on blocked-account opening/unblocking. For student applications, confirm the current minimum amount and accepted evidence from the live Students checklist and Consular Services Portal; do not assume a family support letter from outside Germany is an accepted substitute. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: GOV.UK — Student visa financial requirement and maintenance amounts
sources.note: Availability-only automated check. Verify outstanding course fees, study location, maintenance amount and application-date threshold. HC 584 changes London/outside-London rates from 30 November 2026; cross-check Appendix Student and commencement/transitional rules at lodgement.

sources.name: Home Office — HC 584 Statement of Changes (3 September 2026)
sources.note: Official amendment source. APP ST8–ST10 take effect 30 November 2026 and change maintenance rates to £1,570/month London and £1,203/month outside London; applications made before that date are decided under rules in force on 29 November 2026 for these changes.

sources.name: Home Office — Student and Child Student caseworker guidance (work conditions)
sources.note: Official caseworker guidance for sponsor/course-specific work conditions. Manually verify 20-hour, 10-hour or no-employment categories, term/vacation periods and prohibited work against Appendix Student ST 26 and the student's eVisa conditions.

sources.name: UKVI — Financial evidence for Student and Child Student applicants
sources.note: Official evidence guidance. Verify 28-day holding, 31-day evidence timing, account access and regulation, parent funds/consent, student loan or official sponsorship evidence and nationality differential arrangements.

sources.name: IRCC — Graduate student study permit application and doctoral processing
sources.note: Availability-only automated check. IRCC currently advertises 2-week processing for eligible doctoral students and accompanying family members. Treat as a processing initiative, not a guaranteed service standard or approval. Manually verify current programme eligibility, completeness and live instructions. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: Department of Home Affairs — Student visa family-member inclusion and subsequent entrants (2026 rules)
sources.note: Availability-only automated check. Manually verify exemptions, same-time/same-location requirements, transitional cases and the restriction on adding subsequent entrants after grant. Changes effective 2 October 2026. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: Department of Home Affairs — What applicants and education agents must do under 2026 Student visa application changes
sources.note: Availability-only automated check. Verify onshore/offshore lodgement eligibility, offshore grant-location rule, invalid application risks and transition for applications lodged before 2 October 2026. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: Immigration New Zealand — Student fund requirements
sources.note: Official student maintenance funds, outward travel, tuition payment, sponsorship/financial undertaking and source-of-funds evidence. Tertiary/English/non-compulsory study: NZD 20,000 per year or NZD 1,667 per month for shorter study; verify live rates and applicant-specific sponsor rules.

sources.name: Immigration New Zealand — Post-Study Work Visa
sources.note: Official PSWV requirements, duration, application deadline, NZD 5,000 living funds, online-only application from 16 November 2026, and new Graduate Diploma eligibility. Check exact qualification, time studied in New Zealand, visa history and current instructions.

sources.name: Immigration New Zealand — Qualifications needed for a Post-Study Work Visa
sources.note: Official eligible qualification categories and non-degree Level 4–7 qualification list. Verify exact NZQCF level, full-time study duration and whether employment must be related to the qualification.

sources.name: Immigration New Zealand — New and updated post-study work visa options (16 November 2026)
sources.note: Official announcement: new 6-month Short-Term Graduate Work Visa from 16 November 2026 for eligible Level 5–7 graduates; PSWV extension to Level 7 Graduate Diploma holders who also hold a bachelor's degree; online-only PSWV applications from 16 November. Treat as future-dated until commencement; check exact conditions and transition.

sources.name: Immigration New Zealand — Short-Term Graduate Work Visa
sources.note: Official new visa page; applications open 16 November 2026. Verify NZQCF Level 5–7 qualification, full-time 24-week in-country study, exclusion of English/foundation/bridging/micro-credentials and PSWV-eligible qualifications, 3-month application window, NZD 5,000 funds, no previous PSWV/short-term graduate visa, health/character and employer-only work conditions.

sources.name: Immigration Service Delivery — How to apply for a long-term study visa
sources.note: Official long-stay D study visa route for study over 90 days, application up to 3 months before travel, applicant location, acceptance letter, passport validity, insurance and supporting evidence.

sources.name: Immigration Service Delivery — Information on student finances
sources.note: Official student financial evidence. €10,000 immediate access for academic courses over 8 months, €833/month or €6,665 (whichever lower) for shorter courses; subsequent-year funding, six-month bank histories, sponsor evidence, source-of-funds and approved degree-student education bond.

sources.name: Immigration Service Delivery — ILEP and TrustEd Ireland eligibility
sources.note: Official current provider/course eligibility transition: non-EEA/non-Swiss recruitment only to ILEP-listed or eligible TrustEd-authorised programmes; ILEP closed to new providers, final update 20 June 2025; confirm exact course and provider status.

sources.name: Immigration Service Delivery — Planning to study in Ireland
sources.note: Official course eligibility, full-time study, ILEP/TrustEd, Stamp 2 work conditions and warning that students must support themselves without relying on casual work.

sources.name: Immigration Service Delivery — Immigration permission stamps
sources.note: Official Stamp 2/2A/1G conditions, 20-hour term-time and 40-hour specified vacation work limits, registration within 90 days, and no self-employment/business under Stamp 2/1G.

sources.name: Immigration Service Delivery — Third Level Graduate Programme
sources.note: Official Stamp 1G route for eligible NFQ Level 8 (up to 12 months) and Level 9+ (up to 24 months subject to renewal); current Stamp 2, six-month application deadline, award evidence, time limits and employment conditions.

sources.name: Immigration Service Delivery — Student FAQs
sources.note: Official student guidance on attendance, language-course limits, work hours, family restrictions, fees, insurance, learner protection and student pathway.

sources.name: Quality and Qualifications Ireland — TrustEd Ireland authorised provider reports
sources.note: Official QQI list of higher-education providers authorised to use the statutory TrustEd Ireland quality mark and their assessment reports. Check the exact provider and programme against the current authorised list; the TrustEd Ireland list is replacing the former ILEP as the programme eligibility mechanism.

sources.note: Official student visa route, admission, long-stay visa, 964 annual work-hour limit, indicative fees and study stay information. Manually verify current applicant-specific checklist.

sources.note: Official notice states applications submitted from 1 August 2026 require proof of resources of at least EUR 877.50 per month. Confirm current threshold and application date at lodgement.

sources.note: Official Campus France explanation of the student VLS-TS, 964 hours annual work cap, EEF procedure applicability and online validation within three months.

sources.note: Primary official conditions: IND-recognised sponsor, accredited full-time programme, 50% annual study progress, MVV/residence application process, fee, decision period and student work restrictions.

sources.note: Official accepted proof-of-funds routes, 12-month study norm, own bank account, institution deposit, scholarship, company or private sponsor abroad; includes sponsor statement and recent bank evidence requirements.

sources.note: Official 2026 monthly university/HBO study norm €1,130.77, valid 1 Jan–31 Dec 2026; excludes tuition. Check this live table for annual updates and study category.

sources.note: Official register to verify whether the Dutch education institution is authorised to sponsor international students.

sources.note: Official limited eligibility for the one-year post-study orientation permit, including qualifying Dutch and designated foreign institutions, ranking, IELTS/Nuffic requirements and unrestricted work rights.

sources.name: NetherlandsWorldwide — Dutch representation and appointments
sources.note: Official government portal to confirm current Dutch embassy/consular location, MVV sticker appointment and country-specific instructions for Sri Lankan applicants.

sources.name: Netherlands Labour Authority — Foreign students and work permits
sources.note: Official labour authority guidance: non-EEA students need an employer-arranged TWV and must choose either up to 16 hours weekly or full-time in June, July and August. Programme-integrated internship placement may be exempt where properly documented. Verify current permit and residence conditions before work begins.

sources.name: Italian Embassy Colombo — Study Visa Checklist, version 3/2026
sources.note: Country-specific primary checklist for Sri Lankan applicants, version 3/2026 dated 3 September 2026. Includes 2026/27 financial amount €10,179.85 for university enrolment, 12-month bank statements, sponsor evidence, B2 language, accommodation, insurance and processing up to three months. Verify live checklist and applicant's course category.

sources.name: Universitaly — International student procedures 2026/27 and 2027/28
sources.note: Official coordinated procedures for 2026/27 and 2027/28, Universitaly pre-enrolment categories and national application deadlines. For ordinary Laurea/Laurea Magistrale courses: 30 November 2026 for 2026/27 and 31 October 2027 for 2027/28. Admission/pre-enrolment does not guarantee visa issuance.

sources.name: MAECI — Study in Italy: financial means, residence permit and work
sources.note: Official Ministry guidance: €10,179.85 annual means for university-enrolment study visa for 2026/27 and 2027/28 plus return travel; other visa categories use a different formula; study permit work limit 20 hours/week and 1,040 hours/year; apply for residence permit within 8 days after arrival; work conversion only if study permit remains valid and legal requirements met.

sources.name: Study in Italy — Residence permit procedure for non-EU students
sources.note: Official Study in Italy guidance: non-EU students staying over three months apply for residence permit within 8 working days after arrival; outlines post-office kit and initial supporting documents. Confirm current local Questura and university procedure.

sources.name: Finnish Immigration Service (Migri) — Residence permit application for studies
sources.note: Primary application requirements: eligible study place, first application from abroad, €800/month living funds, €9,600 for one year, private insurance, tuition evidence, Enter Finland and identity verification. Fee displayed on live page: €600 electronic / €750 paper for first adult application; verify at filing.

sources.name: Migri — Income requirement for students
sources.note: Primary financial evidence rules: €800/month or €9,600 for one year; tuition is additional if unpaid; six-month bank statement; funds in applicant's own accessible account; sponsor agreements alone not accepted; origin of family transfers may be requested; institutional free accommodation/meal reductions and scholarship rules.

sources.name: Migri — Students must have insurance
sources.note: Primary student insurance rules: excess no more than €300; at least €120,000 medical expense cover for studies under two years; for studies of two years or more at least €40,000 pharmaceutical expense cover; policy valid on arrival and throughout stay; ordinary short-trip travel insurance not accepted.

sources.name: Migri — Students' right to work
sources.note: Official student work conditions: paid employment in any field average 30 hours/week over the year; degree-related practical training/diploma work may be unrestricted. Verify actual permit and ensure work does not delay studies.

sources.name: Migri — Residence permit to look for work or start a business
sources.note: Official post-study job-search/business route for eligible graduates, up to two years; verify completion status, application timing and current eligibility.

sources.name: Migri — Residence permit based on a degree completed in Finland
sources.note: Official graduate permit route where applicant has completed a Finnish degree and meets job-offer/employment requirements; not automatic on graduation.

Swedish Migration Agency — New higher-education student permit rules from 11 June 2026
Swedish Migration Agency — Permit to look for work after completing studies
Swedish Migration Agency — Extension of higher-education residence permit
Ísland.is — Student residence permit requirements (eligibility, full-time study, funds and insurance)
sources.note: Official Directorate of Immigration requirements. Manually verify 18+ rule, 30 ECTS full-time definition, secure means of support, insurance, criminal record and exact programme eligibility before counselling.

sources.name: Ísland.is — Student residence permit rights and renewal
sources.note: Official rights and renewal page. Manually verify permit duration, renewal, 75% study-progress requirement, 60% work limit, holiday work, family eligibility and post-study routes against current legislation.

sources.name: Directorate of Immigration — 2026 residence and work permit rule changes
sources.note: Official 8 July 2026 amendment notice. Manually verify 75% study progress at every renewal, 60% student employment cap, up to 18-month graduate job-search period and family-reunification scope.

sources.name: Directorate of Immigration — Student permit holders no longer need separate work permits
sources.note: Official 29 June 2026 student employment notice. Verify no separate work permit, maximum 60% of full-time work, full-time work during scheduled academic breaks, self-employment prohibition and first-permit issue-date restriction.

sources.name: Directorate of Immigration — Higher financial support amount from 18 May 2026
sources.note: Official financial benchmark notice. For applications received from 18 May 2026, verify ISK 259,951/month for one individual and the required evidence for the full permit period. Do not assume third-party family sponsorship is accepted.

sources.name: U.S. ICE / SEVP — F-1 student employment (on-campus, CPT and OPT)
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual review required. F-1 on-campus work is generally limited to 20 hours/week while school is in session and may be full-time during official breaks, subject to status and school rules. Off-campus work is not generally free/automatic: CPT must be authorised by the DSO and recorded on Form I-20 before work begins; OPT requires the appropriate DSO recommendation and USCIS employment authorisation/EAD before starting. Check the student's exact F-1 status, programme, timing, I-20 endorsement and current USCIS/ICE rules. Do not promise part-time work or use expected earnings as proof of initial funds. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: U.S. ICE / SEVP — I-901 SEVIS fee and payment FAQ
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manually verify fee and payment timing immediately before advising. ICE currently lists USD 350 for F-1/M-1 students; this is separate from the nonimmigrant visa application fee. Pay only after receiving Form I-20 and use the exact SEVIS ID shown on the current I-20; check the receipt matches that ID. Required fee generally must be paid before the visa interview. Confirm exemptions, repeat-payment rules and current amount on the live ICE FAQ and official payment portal. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: USCIS — Optional Practical Training (OPT) for F-1 students
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual review required. OPT is temporary employment directly related to the student's major area of study, not a job placement or automatic post-study entitlement. Confirm eligibility, DSO recommendation in SEVIS, Form I-765 filing window, USCIS approval and EAD/start date before any work begins. Check unemployment limits, reporting obligations, travel/re-entry and current USCIS instructions. STEM OPT extension is a separate 24-month route with designated STEM degree/CIP code and employer/Form I-983 requirements. Never promise OPT approval or employment. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: Study in Japan — Immigration procedures, COE and financial evidence
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual case review required. Confirm the exact eligible school/course and Student status category; school commonly applies as proxy for the Certificate of Eligibility (COE). Check applicant/guarantor savings balance, income certificate and source-of-funds evidence against the school's current COE checklist and full study budget. COE does not guarantee visa issuance. Confirm current Japan Embassy/VFS Sri Lanka application channel, fees and checklist separately. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: Immigration Services Agency — Student permission for activities outside status (28-hour rule)
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual review required. Student status alone does not permit employment. Confirm advance Permission to Engage in Activity Other Than That Permitted under the Status of Residence (blanket or individual permission). General blanket permission is up to 28 hours per week; during long school holidays up to 8 hours per day. Verify the actual permission endorsement/permit and prohibited activity restrictions; do not treat work permission as automatic or guarantee a job. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: Study in Japan — Part-time work, conditions and income reality-check
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual review required. Official guidance says part-time work requires permission, must not interfere with study, excludes adult-entertainment businesses, and is generally limited to 28 hours weekly or 8 hours daily during long school holidays. Official page reports approximately JPY 81,000 average monthly earnings based on the 2023 survey and warns that part-time work alone cannot cover all tuition and living expenses. Treat survey data as context, not a wage promise. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: Spanish Ministry — Long-term study stay authorisation (Hoja 1)
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual review required. Verify eligible course category, authorised provider, admission/enrolment, minimum in-person attendance where relevant, application timing (generally at least 2 months before start), health insurance, return travel and sufficient funds. Current ministry guidance generally uses 100% of IPREM per month for student maintenance unless accommodation is prepaid for the full stay. Check the current IPREM value and filing-date rules; do not quote an outdated fixed euro amount. Detection is not legal interpretation.

sources.name: Spanish Ministry — Student work access and 30-hour weekly limit (Hoja 4 bis)
sources.note: Availability-only automated check; manual review required. For eligible higher-education study authorisations, work may be automatically permitted where compatible with studies, up to 30 hours per week, subject to applicable geographic and authorisation conditions. Do not apply this generally to all short courses or training categories. Verify current national rules and student's exact authorisation; no job or income guarantee. Detection is not legal interpretation.
